why_null: All four cases in the library were considered and none reached the motif-level threshold. B-01 (casualty-inflation cascade) and B-03 (moral-shock acceleration) both turn on a moral shock propagating from a count of harm or a viral image, and this narrative carries neither a shock nor a count of harm; there is no structural contact. B-02 (fabricated-provision cascade) turns on provisions invented for a legal text whose final wording was not yet public, whereas every node on this spine draws on published figures and the weak point sits in the step between two sourced statements rather than in any invented content. B-04 (scope-inflation panic) is the closest candidate and still falls short: its shape is a rule narrowed in law and widened in the telling, where the widening enlarges the burden the audience expects to carry, while this narrative's shape is a lever priced as sufficient, where the ordering of two sentences removes a burden instead of enlarging one. The two moves run in opposite directions, and the remaining commonality is that both episodes concern a fiscal instrument, which is topic overlap and not motif. B-04 also belongs to the PPN scope-inflation narrative in this set. The claim map already carries the unstated step as the missing edge from the scale node to the funded node, so an Echo panel would add an assertion about a past episode that the library does not support.
